key_insight: The paper proposes a task-conditional faithfulness audit framework that checks whether multimodal LLMs use the right evidence, not just whether they answer correctly.
clinical_relevance: Although focused on power-grid diagnosis rather than medicine, the method is relevant to AI safety in clinical multimodal systems by helping verify evidence-grounded reasoning.
method: Register task-specific evidence requirements before evaluation.
Compare self-reported reliance with behavior under controlled modality ablations.
Use evidence-gated correction and re-audit to regenerate and verify grounded responses.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on three LLMs using IEEE 39-bus and 118-bus grid diagnosis scenarios, showing it can detect and correct faithfulness failures without sacrificing performance.
watch_item: The approach depends on carefully defined evidence requirements and ablation design, so implementation quality may strongly affect whether faithfulness gaps are detected accurately.
paper_title: Task-Conditional Faithfulness Auditing of Multimodal LLMs for Grid Diagnosis
